users.name: Phone user
users.description: A person who runs Shadowsocks on a HarmonyOS NEXT phone. This person adds a server, picks a route, connects, checks traffic, and manages subscriptions.

users.name: HarmonyOS developer
users.description: A developer who ports the Android behavior to the HarmonyOS app. This person reads the control tree, the requirements, and the E2E cases.

problem: The HarmonyOS app is a separate implementation. Android behavior changes do not reach it automatically. No verified list maps each Android screen and control to a HarmonyOS behavior.
outcome: A verified control tree, a requirement set, and an E2E case set. The sets describe the Android mobile app as it behaves at the pinned baseline. Each item states its current HarmonyOS parity.

do: Every page, dialog, menu, and preference screen in the Android mobile module.
Every control that a user can see or operate.
Behavior that the UI exposes, including state changes and validation.
A parity tag for each requirement and each E2E case.
not: Plugin APK internals beyond the UI contract.
Network protocol internals that the UI does not expose.
HarmonyOS implementation work in this version.
later: The a01 requirements model and review batch.
HarmonyOS implementation and UI restoration checks.

assumptions: The pinned Android baseline is the intended parity target.
Android-only surfaces stay Android-only unless HarmonyOS exposes an equivalent system API.
A control that is visible but disabled still counts as a control.
